levels.label: Kids · Beginners

weeks.obj: say hello and goodbye and give their name; follow 3 basic class instructions
weeks.lang: Hello. My name is... Goodbye!; stand up, sit down, look, listen
weeks.res: Music/Songs (hello song); Flashcards/Class rules
weeks.act: Hello circle with names; rehearse attention signal; make the rules poster together
weeks.hw: teach the hello song to someone at home

skills.L: Hello song and attention signal - listen and join in (Music/Songs)
skills.S: Greet the class chorally and say my name in the hello circle
skills.R: Match name cards to faces; find letters in my name (Flashcards)
skills.W: Trace and copy my name; help colour the class-rules poster

lp.wu: Name ball toss: teacher models "Hello, I am Miss/Mister X", each child catches, says their name, throws back. Slow pace, big smiles, no pressure to speak perfectly.
wuAlt: Sit in a circle; roll the ball softly to music, stop music, ball-holder says "My name is..."
Puppet introduces itself to each child; children wave and say hello to the puppet
lp.pres: Present hello/goodbye + 4 instructions (stand up, sit down, look, listen) with giant flashcards and exaggerated modelling. Teach the attention signal ("Hands on head... 1, 2, 3, eyes on me!") and rehearse it 5 times as a game.
presAlt: Puppet show: puppet does right and wrong things; class shouts Yes!/No!
Model and mirror: teacher says + does, children copy like mirrors
lp.prac: Simon Says with the 4 instructions, slow then fast. Then drill "Hello, my name is ___" around the circle with the puppet.
pracAlt: Freeze game: instructions to music, freeze when it stops
Line racing: two teams, first to correctly do the instruction wins a point
lp.ls: Listen and do: teacher calls instructions in random order while children respond; add "touch your nose/head" silliness to check listening honestly.
lp.re: Quick hello circle again · count how many children say their name with confidence; celebrate with a class cheer.
lp.prod: Make the Class Rules Poster together: children add handprints / smiley stickers and practise "We look. We listen." Display it on the wall all year.
lp.rw: Table time: trace names on pre-writing sheets (dotted letters), colour a "Hello" badge to wear home. Fast finishers trace "hello" and "goodbye".
lp.st: Hello Song (Music/Songs) with actions, sung twice; teach the Goodbye Song ready for the end of class. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line (teach it this week).
g: Soft ball, catch-say name-throw. Wrong name? Everyone helps kindly.
Only stand up / sit down / look / listen. Remove "Simon says" later weeks.
Puppet greets each child; child answers or waves · any attempt praised.
Music + instructions; freeze when music stops. Last to freeze is next caller.
Two lines; teacher calls an instruction; first whole line to do it scores.
diff: Fast finishers: write the 4 instruction words on the back of their badge.
Support: name-tracing sheets with larger dotted letters; child may whisper name to puppet first.
hw: Teach the Hello Song to someone at home (family is the audience).
Practise saying "Hello, my name is ___" in front of a mirror 3 times.
Find one English word at home or on packaging and bring it to show the class.
lp.tip: Week 1 is about safety and routine, not English volume. Learn every name before Week 2 · use the register song daily.

weeks.obj: ask How are you? and answer with 4 feeling words
weeks.lang: happy, sad, angry, tired; How are you? I am...
weeks.res: Flashcards (emotions set); Games/Game ideas
weeks.act: Feelings miming game; guess my emotion; feelings board check-in routine
weeks.hw: draw 4 faces and label them

skills.L: Feelings chant - listen and point to the matching face
skills.S: Mime 4 feelings; How are you? circle with flashcards
skills.R: Match feeling words to picture faces
skills.W: Trace feeling words; draw my feeling face

lp.wu: Hello Song + register song from Week 1; children answer "I am here!" with a big smile. Review names with the ball toss at speed.
wuAlt: Feelings weather report: hold up sun/cloud flashcards, children shout happy/sad
Puppet asks each child "How are you?" · puppet answers for shy children first
lp.pres: Present 4 feelings (happy, sad, angry, tired) with the emotions flashcard set: show card, make the face, children copy the face three times. Drill "How are you? · I am happy!"
presAlt: Mirror faces in pairs: one shows a feeling, partner names it
Teacher-story: tell a 30-second story with a feeling; children hold up the right card
lp.prac: Feelings miming: child mimes a feeling, class guesses in English. Then pair drill with the question around the circle.
pracAlt: Flashcard slap: two teams, slap the feeling card the teacher names
Slow reveal: hide card behind a book, slide it up slowly · first correct guess keeps the card
lp.ls: Listen and point: teacher describes ("A boy is sleepy...") children point to the correct flashcard; extend to touch-the-card races.
lp.re: Guess my emotion: teacher pulls a face, children shout the word; then children take turns being the teacher.
lp.prod: Feelings check-in routine: each child puts their name sticker on the feelings chart (happy/sad/angry/tired column) and says "I am ___." This becomes the daily opening routine.
lp.rw: Trace the 4 feeling words (dotted letters); draw and colour own face next to today's feeling. Fast finishers: copy "How are you?"
lp.st: "If You're Happy and You Know It" with all 4 feelings verses (angry = stamp feet, tired = stretch yawn) · Music/Songs. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Mime + guess in English; mime-er chooses next player.
Cards on floor, teams slap the called word. Slow calls first.
Slide card up slowly; earliest correct guesser keeps it.
Match word cards to face cards in pairs · first finished reads them aloud.
Call a feeling + count to 3; everyone makes the statue face.
diff: Fast finishers: match word cards to the flashcards on the wall.
Support: allow pointing before saying; pair a confident child with a quiet one.
hw: Draw 4 faces and label them (happy, sad, angry, tired).
Ask 2 people at home "How are you?" and report back in English words.
Play emotion statues with your family · you are the teacher.
lp.tip: Keep the feelings chart up permanently · it doubles as your daily register and an emotional check-in tool.

weeks.obj: recognize and say 5 colors and answer What color is it?
weeks.lang: red, blue, yellow, green, black; What color is it? It is...; bonus shapes: circle, square, triangle
weeks.res: Flashcards/Shapes-Colours; Music/Songs (Colors Action Song)
weeks.act: Colors relay race; color chant with actions; color touch game
weeks.hw: find 3 things at home in our colors

skills.L: Colors Action Song - listen, point and sing (Music/Songs)
skills.S: What colour is it? pair pointing game
skills.R: Match colour word cards to colour splats
skills.W: Trace colour words and colour the pictures

lp.wu: Hello Song + feelings-chart check-in ("I am happy!"). Quick review of W1-2 with the paddle flashcards.
wuAlt: Colour hunt: "touch something red!" children race to touch colours in the room
I spy with my little eye... something blue (teacher models, children guess)
lp.pres: Present 5 colours (red, blue, yellow, green, black) with the Shapes-Colours flashcards: card + colour + chorus. Ask "What colour is it?" and full answer "It is red."
presAlt: Colour magic: mix paint or transparent films (blue + yellow = green!) while saying the words
Point-and-pause read of a colours picture book
lp.prac: Point-to: "Point to something red" · children find colours in the classroom. Then the Colors Action Song (listen, point, sing) twice.
pracAlt: Colour corners: assign a colour per corner, call a colour, run to the corner
Flashcard slap with colour cards
lp.ls: Listen and colour: teacher says "The apple is red" · children colour prepared fruit/shape sheets with the right crayon (checks real listening).
lp.re: Colour bingo mini-round: each child picks 3 colour cards; teacher pulls colours from a bag; winners shout Bingo!
lp.prod: Team colour collage: each team gets a big paper with their colour name; they cut/glue magazine pictures or draw items of that colour, then present: "It is blue!"
lp.rw: Trace the 5 colour words and colour the splashes correctly. Fast finishers: write the colour of 3 objects in the room.
lp.st: Colors Action Song (Music/Songs) with full-body actions; picture-book colour questions ("What colour is the bear?"). Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line. Bonus: Shapes Song (circle, square, triangle), listen and point only.
g: Colour per corner; call and run; last ones in help call next.
3 cards each, pull from a bag, full-card = Bingo.
"I spy something green..." guess classroom objects.
Teams slap the called colour; add speed rounds.
diff: Fast finishers: spell colour words aloud with a partner.
Support: keep crayons labelled with colour words for matching.
hw: Colour-by-number sheet (2 colours) with labels traced.
Find 3 red things at home and draw them.
Teach the Colors Action Song chorus to your family.
lp.tip: Insist on the full sentence "It is red" from week 3 · the pattern transfers to nearly every later topic.

weeks.obj: follow a simple Halloween story and say 4 themed words
weeks.lang: pumpkin, witch, ghost, candy; simple story frames
weeks.res: Seasonal/Halloween pack
weeks.act: Pumpkin craft; costume charades; trick-or-treat dialogue circle
weeks.hw: Teach the trick-or-treat chant to your family.

skills.L: Halloween story with picture prompts - listen and join in (Seasonal pack)
skills.S: Say 4 themed words; trick-or-treat chant roleplay
skills.R: Match Halloween words to pictures
skills.W: Trace themed words; colour the pumpkin mask

lp.wu: Hello + feelings; colour review round (Lucky Dip of colour cards from the bag).
wuAlt: Simon Says with colours ("Touch something red!")
Colour hunt relay replay from W3
lp.pres: Halloween special: present pumpkin, witch, ghost, candy with the Seasonal pack flashcards + a simple story ("The Little Witch" style) with picture prompts and lots of pausing.
presAlt: Spooky sound box: play sounds (wind, laugh, door); guess the word
Costume show: teacher items (hat, cape) dress a volunteer as each word
lp.prac: Trick-or-treat roleplay: knock on the door (real classroom door), chant "Trick or treat!", receive a (paper) candy, say thank you. Practise the 4 words in the chant.
pracAlt: Spooky statues: witch/ghost/pumpkin poses on the drum beat
Flashcard haunted house: cards hidden around room; find and name each one
lp.ls: Halloween story listen #2: children hold up the correct card each time they hear pumpkin/witch/ghost/candy · active listening to the same story.
lp.re: Pumpkin pass: pass the pumpkin (orange ball) to music; stop = say a Halloween word + make the face/mime.
lp.prod: Make pumpkin masks or paper jack-o-lantern faces (Seasonal pack craft); parade them while chanting the trick-or-treat rhyme.
lp.rw: Trace the 4 Halloween words; colour the pumpkin mask. Fast finishers: copy "Happy Halloween!"
lp.st: Halloween song ("Knock knock, trick or treat" · Music/Songs or Seasonal pack) with the parade. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Sounds guess the word; cards as backup.
Pose per word on the beat.
Real door knocking; chant + thank you.
diff: Fast finishers: write the 4 words; add "bats" and "hat" as bonus words.
Support: mask-making first, words second · success in craft builds courage to speak.
hw: Teach the trick-or-treat chant to your family.
Colour the Halloween sheet and label the 4 words.
Find a Halloween image (book/internet) and bring one word to teach the class.
lp.tip: Culture note for the class: Halloween is "fun scary", not real scary. Keep lights on for sensitive children and check families are comfortable · offer an autumn-pumpkin framing as an alternative. Halloween falls this weekend (31 Oct), so this is the right week for it.

weeks.obj: count 1-10 forwards and catch-count in a circle
weeks.lang: numbers 1-10; How many?
weeks.res: Games/Game ideas (counting games)
weeks.act: Counting chant with fingers; ball circle count; line-up game by number cards
weeks.hw: count the doors and windows at home

skills.L: Listen and count sounds (claps, bells); count along 1-10
skills.S: Catch-count circle; count objects aloud in pairs
skills.R: Match numeral cards to dot cards
skills.W: Trace numbers 1-10; count-and-mark sheets (Worksheets)

lp.wu: Hello Song + feelings chart. Colour review round of Flashcard Slap at speed.
wuAlt: Colour hunt relay: run, touch a called colour, run back
Bingo round with colour cards
lp.pres: Present numbers 1-10 with numeral flashcards: count chorally forwards, then count the class, chairs, pencils · real counting, not just chanting.
presAlt: Counting song with fingers (Music/Songs counting set)
Number line hop: jump along a floor number line saying numbers
lp.prac: Catch-count circle: throw the ball, count in order 1→10, restart at 1; add "How many?" with flashcard dots.
pracAlt: Human numbers: children hold numeral cards and order themselves 1-10
Clap-count: clap the number of claps you hear, then say the number
lp.ls: Listen and count: teacher drops coins/claps behind a screen; children count and hold up the numeral card. Classic, and it truly checks listening.
lp.re: Speed round: count 1-10 as fast as class can, then backwards from 5. Giggle guaranteed.
lp.prod: Counting museum: children collect exactly 5 (then 8, then 10) classroom objects and make a display on their table; partner checks by counting in English.
lp.rw: Trace numerals and number words 1-5 (1 one, 2 two...); count-and-match sheets from Worksheets. Fast finishers: 6-10.
lp.st: Read a counting picture book (10 Little... ) with pause-and-count pages; number song to finish. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Ball toss counting in order; drop = start again (kindly!).
Claps/drops behind a screen; hold up numeral card.
Floor numbers; hop and say; hop backwards = challenge.
Children order themselves with numeral cards.
Partner flashes fingers; other counts and says.
diff: Fast finishers: write 6-10 words; simple sums in English (one and one is two).
Support: numeral cards to hold before saying; count together first.
hw: Count 10 objects at home with a family member · in English.
Trace numbers 1-10 sheet and draw the right dots next to each.
Play Listen & Count with a parent clapping.
lp.tip: Keep Numbers as the main lesson. Green March (6 Nov) falls this week: the optional map craft is in the Occasion note.

occ.act: Map craft: colour the march route and say "the march goes to..."; flag colours chant.

weeks.obj: combine colors and numbers in color-by-number work
weeks.lang: review: colors + 1-10; How many (red) balloons?
weeks.res: Worksheets/Print outs; Games/Printable games
weeks.act: Color-by-number worksheet; team quiz; fast-finisher extension cards
weeks.hw: Teach someone at home 3 words from this week (Colors + numbers review) and show them the gesture.

skills.L: Listen for colour + number (three red balloons) and hold up cards
skills.S: How many red balloons? team guessing game
skills.R: Colour-by-number instructions read together
skills.W: Colour-by-number sheet; trace number words

lp.wu: Hello + feelings routine; speed count 1-10; one Colour Corners round to shake out energy.
wuAlt: Number bingo warm-up
"Point to something blue" quick commands round
lp.pres: Combine colours + numbers: "How many red balloons?" with flashcards of balloon bunches. Model answer "Three red balloons."
presAlt: Real balloons or counters in colours: count and describe together
Picture pairs: show two cards, class compares (3 blue / 2 red)
lp.prac: Color-by-number work (Worksheets): teacher calls the code ("1 is red, 2 is blue"), children colour by number · the flagship activity of this week.
pracAlt: Dice colour game: roll, count, colour that many circles in the rolled colour
"Grab 3 yellow" · teacher calls number+colour, children grab counters
lp.ls: Teacher describes a hidden picture ("I see four green frogs...") children build/draw it correctly · listening with colours + numbers combined.
lp.re: Quick quiz: teacher holds up dots of a colour, class asks "How many?" and answers as a chorus.
lp.prod: Balloon picture factory: each child draws a bunch of coloured balloons with a number label, then presents: "Five red balloons!" Display on the wall gallery.
lp.rw: Complete colour-and-number sentences: "___ red balloons" (write the number word); matching sheets from Worksheets/Print outs.
lp.st: Revisit the Colors Action Song + counting song as a medley; children choose the order · choice = engagement. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Roll dice, count, colour circles in your colour.
Call number + colour; grab counters; verify together.
Same sheet, teams; correct colouring wins.
Listen to description; draw/build it right.
Hold up dot cards; class asks and answers.
diff: Fast finishers: write the full sentence "I have three red balloons."
Support: pre-counted counters; colour-word wall chart for reference.
hw: Finish the colour-by-number picture and bring it for the gallery.
Count and colour: 3 blue things, 5 red things at home.
Teach someone the balloon sentence with your drawing.
lp.tip: This is the consolidation week · no new vocabulary. Raising accuracy and confidence on old language beats adding new.

weeks.obj: name 6 classroom objects and ask for them politely
weeks.lang: pen, pencil, book, bag, chair, table; Can I have..., please?
weeks.res: Flashcards (school subjects/objects set)
weeks.act: Point-and-say scavenger hunt; What is missing? tray game
weeks.hw: label 3 objects at home (with family help)

skills.L: Listen to Can I have... please requests and do as I say
skills.S: Ask for classroom objects politely in a shop-corner game
skills.R: Match object words to labelled picture cards (Flashcards)
skills.W: Label desk objects with word cards; trace object words

lp.wu: Hello + feelings; quick balloon-picture gallery tour · 3 children present their homework sentences.
wuAlt: Object hunt: "Bring me a pencil... a book!" realia round
Lucky dip: pull an object from the bag, name it if you can
lp.pres: Present 6 classroom objects (pen, pencil, book, bag, chair, table) with real objects + flashcards: touch, say, pass around the circle.
presAlt: Mystery bag: feel inside, guess the object, reveal
Label the classroom: children stick word cards on real objects
lp.prac: "Can I have the ___, please?" polite requests: model with the puppet shop; children request objects to build a tower or complete a picture.
pracAlt: Pass the parcel with an object; when music stops, holder asks for it politely
Object swap circles: two circles turn opposite ways; on stop, request partner's object
lp.ls: Listen and fetch: teacher describes ("It is on the table. It is blue. You write with it.") children race to bring the right object.
lp.re: Pencil-case inventory: pairs empty pencil cases and name everything they can in English; count objects for number review.
lp.prod: Classroom shop: half the class are shopkeepers with objects, half are buyers with polite requests; swap roles. Best manners win the "Please Cup".
lp.rw: Label-and-trace sheets: match word cards to object pictures; trace all 6 words. Fast finishers: copy "Can I have a pencil, please?"
lp.st: School objects song (Music/Songs); or "This is my pencil" pass-the-object chant. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Feel, guess, reveal; keep it if right.
Description race to bring the right object.
Stick word cards on real objects; read the room after.
Pairs name + count their pencil cases.
diff: Fast finishers: write the 6 words from memory; check with the wall labels.
Support: picture + word matching first, then tracing.
hw: Label 3 objects at home with paper labels (pen, book, bag...).
Play Mystery Bag with a family member using a pencil case.
Trace and draw the 6 classroom objects sheet.
lp.tip: Real objects beat flashcards this week · the whole lesson can run with a pencil case and a school bag.

occ.act: Flag craft + "I am from Morocco" chant; national symbols matching game.
occ.hw: Teach someone at home the independence chant.

weeks.obj: recognize and say the sounds of letters A-F with 1 word each
weeks.lang: letter-sound links A-F; a is for apple...
weeks.res: Music/Songs (phonics songs); Flashcards
weeks.act: Letter hunt around the room; sound-action pairing; tracing big letters in the air
weeks.hw: trace worksheet A-F (Worksheets)

skills.L: Phonics songs A-F - listen, sing, do the actions (Music/Songs)
skills.S: Say letter sounds A-F with the a-is-for-apple chant
skills.R: Match letters A-F to first-sound pictures (Flashcards)
skills.W: Trace and write letters A-F; first-sound matching sheet

lp.wu: Hello + feelings; classroom object words echo round (say it if you remember it).
wuAlt: Alphabet march: march and chant A B C to the song beat (pre-exposure)
Quick object lucky dip
lp.pres: ABC phonics 1 (letters A-F): present each letter with its sound + anchor word (a-apple, b-ball, c-cat, d-dog, e-elephant, f-fish) using the phonics song and flashcards.
presAlt: Letter-of-the-moment show: big card, trace it in the air with your arm/foot/nose
Mystery letter bag: pull a letter, everyone shouts the sound and word
lp.prac: Air writing + table writing with fingers; then first-sound matching: apple picture → which letter? (picture cards + letter cards).
pracAlt: Letter jump: letter cards on floor; teacher says the sound; jump to it
Sound sort: sort picture cards under A-F letter headers
lp.ls: Phonics song listening: hold up the letter card when you hear its sound in the song (pre-teach: cards ready, listen, raise!).
lp.re: Quick-fire: teacher shows a letter, class makes the sound + word; reverse: teacher says the word, class finds the letter.
lp.prod: Letter detectives: find A-F letters in classroom print (posters, books, labels) with magnifying-glass fingers; tally how many of each letter they find.
lp.rw: Trace and write A-F (lower + upper case) on phonics sheets (Worksheets); draw the anchor word next to each letter.
lp.st: Phonics song (Music/Songs) again as a sing-along; start building the class Letter Wall (each week adds letters). Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Sound called, jump to the letter card.
Hunt letters in classroom print; tally.
Write letters in air with elbow/knee; partner guesses.
diff: Fast finishers: match 2 words per letter (a: apple, ant).
Support: letter cards with the anchor picture printed on them as a bridge.
hw: Find 3 things at home that start with b, c, or d (say them in English).
Trace A-F sheet; colour the anchor words.
Sing the phonics song to family; teach them one action.
lp.tip: Say sounds ("b is /b/"), never letter names yet · "bee" comes in W24's alphabet song. Keep anchors consistent all year (same apple, same cat).

occ.act: Gratitude turkey craft: one feather = one "I am thankful for..." sentence.
occ.hw: Say 3 "I am thankful for..." sentences at home.

weeks.obj: match letters G-M to their sounds and first-letter pictures
weeks.lang: letter-sound links G-M
weeks.res: Music/Songs; Flashcards
weeks.act: Letter crafts; first-sound sorting game; alphabet line-up
weeks.hw: find one object per letter G-M (any 3)

skills.L: Phonics songs G-M; listen and hold up the letter card
skills.S: Sound relay - hear the sound, say the letter and word
skills.R: Match letters G-M to pictures; sort by first sound
skills.W: Trace letters G-M; write the missing first letter

lp.wu: Hello + feelings; A-F quick-fire sound round with flashcards.
wuAlt: Letter Jump replay at speed
Detective tally share: who found the most letters at home
lp.pres: ABC phonics 2 (G-M): same routine · g-goat, h-hat, i-igloo, j-jam, k-kite, l-lion, m-monkey · song, cards, actions.
presAlt: Add actions per letter (goat butts, monkey scratches); class invents the action · invented actions stick best
Letter story: one silly sentence per letter ("The goat eats jam!")
lp.prac: First-letter pictures: match picture cards to G-M letters; then mix A-M for cumulative sorting (this recycling is the point).
pracAlt: Letter Slap: two teams slap the letter whose sound is made
Pass the letter: music pass a card; stop = sound + word + action
lp.ls: Beginning-sound bingo: teacher says a word ("monkey!"); children cover the letter m on their bingo card.
lp.re: A-M speed parade: letters in order round the circle, each child one letter; restart with a shuffle · can the class do it in 13 seconds?
lp.prod: Letter Wall building: children add G-M cards + pictures to the class Letter Wall and "read the wall" chorally (a: apple... m: monkey).
lp.rw: Trace G-M sheets; missing-letter sheets ( _at → hat with picture support). Fast finishers: write 3 G-M words from the wall.
lp.st: Phonics song medley A-M with all the actions the class invented. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Sound made, team slaps the letter.
Circle order A-M against the clock.
Do the invented action; class says letter + word.
Make "goat eats jam" sentences; act them out.
diff: Fast finishers: 3-letter reading prep · blend c-a-t with you one-to-one.
Support: keep A-F cards visible during G-M work; confusion is normal at this stage.
hw: Find one object at home for g, h, or m and bring the word.
Trace G-M sheet + colour anchor words.
Teach your family the letter actions for 3 letters.
lp.tip: Cumulative review every week now: A-M mixed, not just the new seven. Five minutes of old letters beats twenty of new ones.

weeks.obj: name 5 family members and say This is my...
weeks.lang: mother, father, sister, brother, baby; This is my...
weeks.res: Flashcards/Family; Music/Songs (Family Song)
weeks.act: Family tree drawing; family song with finger play; show-and-tell photo moment
weeks.hw: draw your family tree

skills.L: Family Song - listen and point to family members (Music/Songs)
skills.S: Introduce family photos: This is my mummy
skills.R: Match family words to a family picture (Flashcards/Family)
skills.W: Trace family words; draw my family and label it

lp.wu: Hello + feelings; A-M letter parade; one Sound Sort round mixing all letters.
wuAlt: Family song chorus as a pre-listen
Letter Slap championship round
lp.pres: My family: present mother, father, sister, brother, baby with the Family flashcards + Family Song. Model "This is my mother." with family photos of teacher (real photos are gold).
presAlt: Finger family puppets: draw faces on fingers, present each member
Story book family: a picture-book family is presented; children point to members
lp.prac: Family Song with finger puppets (Music/Songs); then card drill: show card, class says "This is my sister."
pracAlt: Family photo circle: children who brought photos show and say one line
Guess who: hide a card; children guess which family member is missing
lp.ls: Listen and build: teacher describes a family ("The baby is little. The sister is tall."); children arrange family cards or draw the family correctly.
lp.re: Family chant with rhythm: clap-clap "mother!", clap-clap "father!" · speed rounds.
lp.prod: My family drawing: children draw their family and rehearse one line per person ("This is my father.") in pairs; volunteers present to the class.
lp.rw: Trace family words; label the family drawing (mummy, daddy...). Fast finishers: copy "This is my family."
lp.st: Family Song full sing-along + a family-themed picture book read-aloud. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Draw faces on fingers; song drives the drill.
Cards face down; remove one; guess in English.
Show photo, say one line, pass on.
diff: Fast finishers: add grandfather/grandmother as bonus words.
Support: sentence frame card "This is my ___" stays on the board all lesson.
hw: Finish the family drawing and label 3 people in English.

pracAlt: Speed meeting: two circles, inner and outer, rotate every 40 seconds with the same 3 questions
Spelling pair game: one child spells a name, the partner writes it and checks
lp.ls: Teacher reads three short introductions aloud (no recording needed): 'Hi, I'm Sami. I'm ten. I'm from Nador.' Children tick the matching fact card (name, age, town). Read each twice; check in pairs.
lp.re: Instruction Simon Says with 8 classroom instructions (open your book, close your book, stand up, sit down, look, listen, write, read). Speed up; then a child becomes Simon.
lp.prod: Introduce your partner: each child stands and says 3 sentences about the partner from the fact card ('This is Rim. She's nine. She's from Berkane.'). Display the cards as a Class Gallery.
lp.rw: Read a 4-line introduction card, then complete the frame My name is ___. I'm ___. I'm from ___. Copy and spell the name correctly. Fast finishers write a 4th sentence ('I like...').
lp.st: Hello and goodbye song of choice from Music/Songs; then a quick round: 'Goodbye, see you next week!' Goodbye: exit ticket, each child says one new sentence at the door.
g: Each child repeats all the earlier names and adds their own.
Only follow instructions that start with 'Simon says'.
Collect names and ages on a grid by asking questions.
Teams spell a name aloud and a runner writes it on the board.
Two rotating circles practise the same 3 questions.
diff: Fast finishers: write a second fact card about a famous person and read it out.
Support: use the sentence frame on the board and the alphabet strip; allow a partner to whisper the answer first.
hw: Write 3 sentences about yourself and read them to someone at home.
Teach the family the question 'How do you spell it?' and spell 3 names.
Draw yourself and label your name, age and town.
lp.tip: Learn every name this week and check each child's level quietly: who can already answer, who only repeats. Keep the corrections kind and short. Cambridge Global English 1 (Starter and Unit 1) is a good reference for this theme.

weeks.obj: name 10 countries and nationalities; say where I and others are from and what languages I speak; ask and answer Where are you from? and What languages do you speak?; describe a flag with colours
weeks.lang: Morocco, Algeria, Spain, France, Egypt, Turkey, the USA, Britain, Japan, Brazil; Moroccan, Algerian, Spanish, French, Egyptian, Turkish, American, British, Japanese, Brazilian; Where are you from? I'm from Morocco. I'm Moroccan.; What languages do you speak? I speak Arabic, French and English.; Is he from Spain? Yes, he is. / No, he isn't.; The flag is red and green.
weeks.res: Countries hidden picture game (PPT); All country flags in one flag (video)
weeks.act: Flag fact files: each group presents a country (flag colours, nationality, language) and plays a 'Where is he from?' guessing game
weeks.hw: Make a fact card about a country you like: name, nationality, flag colours and one language (4 sentences).

skills.L: Listen to children introducing themselves and match them to countries on a map
skills.S: Ask and answer Where are you from? and What languages do you speak?
skills.R: Read a short fact file about a country and answer 4 questions
skills.W: Write 4 sentences about a country with from, flag colours and language

lp.wu: Flag flash: show a flag for 3 seconds and children say the country; then 'Stand up if you speak Arabic... French... English!' Teacher models 'I speak Arabic and French.'
wuAlt: Country chain: each child says a country that starts with the last letter of the previous one
Map point: the teacher says a country and children point on the wall map
lp.pres: Present the 10 countries and nationalities with flag cards on a world map (use the Countries hidden picture PPT or the flag video). Model 'Where are you from? I'm from Morocco. I'm Moroccan.' Mark the stress on the nationality suffix (Moroccan, Spanish, American). Teach 'I speak...' with a language chart.
presAlt: Flag match: match flag cards to country and nationality cards
Passport game: each child gets a card with a name, country and languages and introduces themselves
lp.prac: Passport interview: children receive passport cards (name, country, nationality, languages) and walk and ask 'Where are you from? What languages do you speak?' until they have met 5 people, then report 'Sofia is from Spain. She's Spanish. She speaks Spanish and English.'
pracAlt: Is he from...? Hot seat: a child wears a country card and the class asks yes/no questions
Information gap: partners with half a world table ask Where is Emma from?
lp.ls: Teacher reads four short introductions aloud (no recording needed): 'Hi, I'm Kenji. I'm from Japan. I speak Japanese and English.' Children match each speaker to a flag and a language on a worksheet. Read twice and check in pairs.
lp.re: Flag bingo: cover the flag for the country or nationality the teacher calls; the winner reads the card aloud and says 'It's red and white. It's Turkey.'
lp.prod: Country fact file poster: in groups, choose a country, draw the flag, label the colours and write 4 sentences ('This is Brazil. The people are Brazilian. They speak Portuguese. The flag is green and yellow.'). Present to another group, who ask 2 questions.
lp.rw: Read a 5-line fact file about Spain and answer 4 questions (Where is she from? What does she speak?). Then write 4 sentences about your country. Fast finishers add a second country and compare the flags.
lp.st: Country song or flag video from Videos/Videos for Children/Countries/Culture (all country flags), then a quick 'Hello' greeting in three languages. Goodbye: exit ticket, each child says one new sentence at the door.
g: Say the country of the flag shown for 3 seconds.
Meet 5 people and report where they are from.
Say a country starting with the last letter of the previous one.
Cover the flag or nationality that is called.
Guess the country card by asking yes/no questions.
diff: Fast finishers: write a 6-line text about a famous person and their country and nationality.
Support: use flag cards with country and nationality words side by side and the frame I'm from ___. I'm ___.
hw: Make a fact card about a country you like (4 sentences).
Ask someone at home what languages they speak and write it in English.
Draw 3 flags and write the colours.
lp.tip: Many children have relatives abroad: invite them to share. Keep it positive and avoid politics; stay with flags, languages and greetings. Cambridge Global English 2 (Unit 2: places in the world) is a good reference.

weeks.obj: say the 12 months and ordinals first to twelfth; say and write dates (the fifth of May); ask and answer When is your birthday? and How old are you?; make a class birthday chart
weeks.lang: January to December; first, second, third, fourth, fifth... twelfth; When is your birthday? It's on the fifth of May. / It's in May.; How old are you? I'm nine. / I'm ten next week.; Happy birthday! / Thank you!
weeks.res: Ordinal numbers game (PPT); Learn months in English (video game)
weeks.act: Class birthday calendar: interview 8 classmates, put them on a month chart and report 'Amina's birthday is on the third of June.'
weeks.hw: Write the birthdays of 5 people in your family (for example, My mum's birthday is on the tenth of April).

skills.L: Listen to dates and write them on a calendar
skills.S: Ask and answer When is your birthday? and How old are you?
skills.R: Read a short text about a birthday party and answer 4 questions
skills.W: Write dates and 4 sentences about birthdays

lp.wu: Months of the year: pass a ball and say the next month; teacher calls 'Birthday month!' and children in that month stand and say 'My birthday is in May.' Next, the birthday line-up in order without speaking.
wuAlt: Month chant with a clap pattern
Calendar race: teams stick month cards in order
lp.pres: Present the 12 months on the months wheel and ordinals first to twelfth with a number line (1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th...). Show the date pattern 'It's on the fifth of May' and the short 'It's in May.' Model 'When is your birthday?' and 'How old are you?' Stress the th endings with a mouth gesture.
presAlt: Ordinals line: 12 children hold cards and call positions (first, second...)
Date dictation: teacher says dates, children write 5th, 12th, 3rd
lp.prac: Birthday survey: each child interviews 8 classmates ('When is your birthday?') and records the date on a grid, then sticks names on a class month chart. Groups report: 'There are three birthdays in May. Sara's birthday is on the second of May.'
pracAlt: Missing dates: pairs complete a half calendar by asking partners
Find someone who: whose birthday is in winter, in the first week of a month?
lp.ls: Teacher reads aloud (no recording needed): 'My birthday is on the fourth of June. My sister's birthday is on the twelfth of March. My dad's is on the first of January.' Children write the dates on a calendar and say who is the oldest in the family order. Repeat with 3 more people.
lp.re: Birthday bingo: each child has a card with 9 dates (5th May, 2nd June...) and covers the date the teacher says; winners read a line aloud.
lp.prod: Make a Birthday Calendar poster for the class: draw a cake for each month, add names and ordinal dates and present 'Amina is the first in January.' Add a birthday card for a classmate: 'Happy birthday, Omar! You are ten.'
lp.rw: Read a 5-line text about Lina's party ('Lina's birthday is on the ninth of May. She is ten...') and answer 4 questions. Then write 4 sentences with dates. Fast finishers write the date today and tomorrow in full.
lp.st: Song 'Happy Birthday' with the class's birthday child, or the video 'Learn Months In English' from Games/Video games. Goodbye: exit ticket, each child says one new sentence at the door.
g: Line up in birthday order without speaking.
Stick month cards on the right place in order.
Write the dates the teacher says.
Complete a calendar by asking questions.
diff: Fast finishers: write a short invitation for a birthday party with date and place.
Support: ordinals chart on the wall; calendar with months and numbers filled in.
hw: Write the birthdays of 5 people in your family.
Make a calendar page for your birthday month.
Teach someone the months in English.
lp.tip: Ordinals and months are tricky: many dates are written differently at home. Ask for birthday months only; children may prefer not to share the exact day. Check that no child is excluded by cake or party talk.

weeks.theme: My day: daily routine and time
weeks.obj: say the time (o'clock and half past); describe my daily routine with I get up/have breakfast at...; ask and answer What time do you get up? with times; order a routine with first, then, after that
weeks.lang: get up, wash my face, brush my teeth, have breakfast, go to school, have lunch, do homework, go to bed; It's seven o'clock. / It's half past eight.; What time do you get up? I get up at seven o'clock.; first, then, after that, in the morning/afternoon/evening
weeks.res: Daily routine flashcards; Daily routines and simple time (PPT with pool game); Telling the time worksheets; What's the time, Mr Wolf? (printable game); Telling the time flashcards (PDF)
weeks.act: Daily routine cards: order and tell the routine with times and a class survey on wake-up time
weeks.hw: Write 5 sentences about your daily routine with times ('I get up at 7. I go to school at 8.').

skills.L: Listen to a routine and match times to pictures
skills.S: Ask and answer What time do you...? and tell my routine
skills.R: Read a short routine text and answer 4 questions
skills.W: Write 5 sentences about my daily routine with times

lp.wu: What's the time, Mr Wolf? game: the teacher says 'It's three o'clock' and children take 3 steps; 'Dinner time!' means run. Practise o'clock and half past with a clock face.
wuAlt: Clock faces: show the time on a paper clock
Morning chant with actions (get up, wash, brush)
lp.pres: Present the routine verbs with the Daily Routine flashcards and clock faces for o'clock and half past. Model 'What time do you get up? I get up at seven o'clock. I have breakfast at half past seven.' and 'first, then, after that'. Present simple with I only. Teacher also shows 'She gets up at 7' (chunk).
presAlt: Routine ordering: put cards in order with times
Time matching: clock faces and sentences
lp.prac: Routine interview: pairs ask 'What time do you get up? What time do you go to school?' and fill in a time chart. Then they tell the class a partner's routine in 3 sentences (I use 'He gets up at...' as chunks).
pracAlt: Information gap: partners with different routine charts ask What time...?
Routine mime: mime a routine action and say the time
lp.ls: Teacher reads aloud (no recording needed): 'I get up at seven o'clock. I have breakfast at half past seven. I go to school at eight o'clock.' Children draw the hands on clock faces and number the pictures. Repeat with a second routine.
lp.re: Time bingo: cover the clock that shows the time the teacher says. Then 'Sleeping lions': children lie down until the teacher says a time and an action.
lp.prod: Make a 'My day' poster: draw 6 routine pictures with clock faces and sentences ('I get up at 7 o'clock.'). Present in groups, then compare: 'We both go to bed at nine.'
lp.rw: Read a 6-line routine text (Sara's day) and answer 4 questions with times. Then write 5 sentences about your day. Fast finishers add first, then, after that, and a weekend routine.
lp.st: Song 'Wake Up! Daily Routines Song' or 'Good Morning Song' from Music/Songs. Goodbye: exit ticket, each child says one new sentence at the door.
g: Take steps for the time the wolf says.
Show the time on a clock for the teacher to check.
Order the picture cards with times.
Cover the clock for the time called.
Lie down until the teacher says a time and an action.
diff: Fast finishers: write a weekend routine with 6 sentences and times.
Support: clock face stamps with a word list; use cards with times already written.
hw: Write 5 sentences about your daily routine with times.
Make a clock from paper and show 5 times to someone at home.
Ask a family member what time they get up and write it.
lp.tip: Present simple with I and you only; he/she -s is a chunk. Telling time to o'clock and half past is enough. Keep a time chart on the wall and ask 'What time is it?' in the hello step. Halloween is an optional overlay this week.

weeks.theme: School subjects and days of the week
weeks.obj: name 8 school subjects and the 7 days; say what I have on each day and what I like; ask and answer What day is it? What have we got on Monday?

weeks.act: Make and present a personal weekly timetable, then ask partners about their favourite subjects
weeks.hw: Write your timetable for 3 days: 'On Monday I've got ___ and ___.' Say it at home.

skills.L: Listen to timetable sentences and write the subject in the correct day
skills.S: Ask and answer What day is it? and What have we got on...?
skills.R: Read a short timetable text and answer 3 questions
skills.W: Write a 3-day timetable and 3 sentences about my favourite subjects

lp.wu: Days chant: say Monday to Sunday with a clap pattern; take away one day each round and let children say the missing day. End with 'What day is it today?'
wuAlt: Day line-up: 7 children hold day cards and the others order them
Yesterday and tomorrow: teacher says 'Today is Tuesday. Tomorrow is...?'
lp.pres: Present the subjects with the School subjects flashcards and the timetable card. Model 'What have we got on Monday? We've got English and Maths.' and 'I like Art. My favourite subject is Science.' Practise as a chorus, then by days.
presAlt: Subject mime: mime a subject, the class guesses
Timetable race: teams put subject cards in the right day columns
lp.prac: Timetable interview: pairs ask each other 'What have you got on Wednesday?' and fill in a blank timetable. Then compare: 'We both have Art on Tuesday.'
pracAlt: Information gap: each partner has half a timetable and asks questions to complete it
Guess my day: 'I've got PE and Music. What day is it?'
lp.ls: Teacher reads a simple class timetable aloud (no recording needed): 'On Monday we've got Arabic, Maths and PE. On Tuesday we've got English...' Children write the subjects under the right day on a blank grid.
lp.re: Subject bingo and 'Who is it?' questions: Teacher says a child's favourite subject and a day; the class guesses who it is from the class poll.
lp.prod: Make My Perfect Week poster: each child writes a timetable for 3 days with their favourite subjects and presents it: 'On Friday I've got Art and PE. I like Art.'
lp.rw: Read a text about a child's school day (Sara's timetable) and answer 3 questions. Then write 3 sentences about your timetable. Fast finishers add 'I don't like...' for one subject.
lp.st: Song 'School' or a days of the week chant from Music/Songs / Videos. Goodbye: exit ticket, each child says one new sentence at the door.
g: Say the day that was taken away from the chant.
Order day cards on the floor.
Mime a subject for others to guess.
Teams put subject cards on the right days.
Guess a child from their favourite subject and day.
diff: Fast finishers: write a dialogue between two children about the week.
Support: use a printed timetable with pictures; copy the sentence frames.
hw: Write your timetable for 3 days and say it at home.
Make a days of the week song or rap and teach someone.
Interview someone at home: what is their favourite day?
lp.tip: Days of the week are used all year: keep a days chart on the wall. Link to Week 4: 'What time is English? It's at nine o'clock.' Green March is an optional overlay this week.

weeks.theme: Jobs and people who help us
weeks.obj: name 12 jobs; say what people do and where they work (He's a doctor. He works in a hospital.); ask and answer What does he/she do? and Where does she work?; say what I want to be
weeks.lang: teacher, doctor, nurse, baker, farmer, driver, police officer, firefighter, cook, shopkeeper, mechanic, pilot; hospital, school, bakery, farm, shop, garage, airport; What does your mum do? She's a nurse.; Where does he work? He works in a hospital.; I want to be a pilot.
weeks.res: Jobs flashcards; Jobs and occupations hidden picture game (PPT); Jobs and occupations ESL game (video)
weeks.act: Job riddles and a 'Who helps us?' poster: describe a job without saying it for others to guess
weeks.hw: Write about 3 people you know (family or neighbours): 'My uncle is a driver. He works in a bus.'

skills.L: Listen to job descriptions and match them to the picture
skills.S: Ask and answer What does he/she do? and Where does she work?
skills.R: Read a short text about people at work and answer 4 questions
skills.W: Write 4 sentences about jobs, places and what I want to be

lp.wu: Job mime: a child mimes a job and the class guesses 'Are you a baker?' Teacher models 'No, I'm not. I'm a cook.' Add the song 'Who works in the...?'
wuAlt: Uniform match: the teacher holds up a hat or tool and children say the job
Silent mime relay in teams
lp.pres: Present the jobs with the Jobs flashcards and the Jobs hidden picture PPT. Model 'He's a doctor. He works in a hospital. He helps sick people.' with a pair of pictures: person + place. Practise the question 'What does he do? Where does she work?' and the wish 'I want to be a pilot.'
presAlt: Job and place match cards (doctor - hospital, baker - bakery)
Sentence builders: build 'She is a teacher. She works in a school.'
lp.prac: Who am I? in pairs: Child A has a job card and gives 3 clues ('I work in a hospital. I wear white. I help people.'), Child B asks 'Are you a doctor?' and guesses. Swap, then do 'What does your mum/dad do?' with real families.
pracAlt: Information gap: partners have half a job table and ask What does he do? Where does he work?
Interview a classmate about who they want to be
lp.ls: Teacher reads three short riddles aloud (no recording needed): 'I work in a kitchen. I wear a white hat. I make food. What do I do?' Children point to the right job card. Then four people describe their workplace and children match them to places.
lp.re: Job charades in teams: a child mimes the job and the team says 'You are a firefighter!' The team must also say where the person works.
lp.prod: Make a 'People who help us' poster: groups choose 4 jobs, draw them and write 2 sentences each ('A nurse works in a hospital. She helps sick people.'). Present to another group and answer 'What does a farmer do?'
lp.rw: Read a 5-line text about Karim's family ('My dad is a driver. He works in a bus...') and answer 4 questions. Then write 4 sentences about people you know. Fast finishers write what they want to be and why with 'because' (optional).
lp.st: Song 'Jobs Song' or 'People work' from Music/Songs. Goodbye: exit ticket, each child says one new sentence at the door.
g: Give 3 clues about a job and the partner guesses.
Mime a job and say where the person works.
Name the job from a hat or tool.
Match jobs to the places where they work.
Build job sentences from word cards.
diff: Fast finishers: write a mini interview with a person at work (4 questions and answers).
Support: job and place picture pairs; sentence frame She's a ___. She works in a ___.
hw: Write about 3 people you know and what they do.
Draw yourself in your dream job and write one sentence.
Ask someone at home what they do and write it in English.
lp.tip: Be sensitive to families where an adult is not working: use 'a person in my street' or a character card. Include local jobs: baker, fisherman, tailor, mechanic. Labour Day (1 May) comes in Week 30 as an optional overlay.

Yes, he has. / No, he hasn't.; What is she like? She's funny.

skills.S: Describe a person and ask Has he/she got...? What is she like?

wuAlt: Mirror faces in pairs: describe what you see
Personality charades: act kind, shy, funny and guess
lp.pres: Present face and hair words and the personality adjectives with pictures and mini role plays. Model 'He's got short black hair and brown eyes. He's tall. He's kind.' and 'What is she like? She's funny.' Stress has got for looks and is for personality. Chorus, then pairs.

Match: face cards with descriptions

pracAlt: Guess who? Each child has a grid of faces and asks Has he got...? until the face is found
Odd one out: 4 faces, 3 have curly hair - say which one is different
lp.ls: Teacher reads aloud (no recording needed): 'My friend Nora has got long straight black hair and brown eyes. She's tall and kind. She hasn't got glasses.' Children choose the correct picture out of 3 and tick the personality adjectives. Do it twice.
lp.re: Guess who in teams: the teacher thinks of a child, the teams ask up to 5 yes/no questions (Has he got short hair? Is she funny?). The first team to say the name scores.
lp.prod: Create a character: draw a hero or friend from a description, then present: 'This is Zayd. He's got three eyes and long green hair. He's very tall and funny.' The class draws and checks.
lp.rw: Read a 5-line description of a person and match it to the right picture. Then write 5 sentences about a person you love. Fast finishers write 2 questions (Has she got...? What is she like?).
lp.st: Song 'Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes' (fast) or 'My Body' from Music/Songs. Goodbye: exit ticket, each child says one new sentence at the door.
g: Draw a character from a partner's description.
Ask Has he got...? to find the secret face.
Act a personality word for the class to guess.
Find the face that is different and explain.
Describe your partner's face and hair.
diff: Fast finishers: write a full paragraph about a famous person (6 sentences).
Support: a picture word bank for hair, eyes and personality; sentence frames He's got ___. She's ___.
hw: Describe a person you love in 5 sentences and draw them.
Play Guess who? at home with 3 clues.
Write 6 personality words and act them for someone at home.
lp.tip: Has got (appearance) vs is (personality) is the real step: colour-code them. Do not comment on children's bodies: describe pictures, characters and loved ones. Body words are reviewed from Beginners and recycled here.

weeks.obj: say the 5 short vowel sounds, blend and read 20 CVC words, and read 6 short sentences aloud; write 5 CVC words from dictation

Word wheel: spin the wheel, blend the word and check with a picture
lp.prac: Blend-and-read relay: teams run to the board, read a CVC word aloud and match it to a picture. Then read 6 sentence cards (The cat is on the mat.) in pairs and act them.
pracAlt: Picture-word pairs: match CVC picture cards to word cards
Read and act: read a sentence card (Sit on the mat) and do the action
lp.ls: Teacher says 10 CVC words (no recording needed): 'cat, pet, pig, hot, sun...' Children listen and hold up the vowel letter card for the middle sound. Then 5 words are dictated for writing.
lp.re: Quick-write whiteboards: teacher says a CVC word, children write it, hold up and say it; correct words score a point. Follow with a 'sound sort' of picture cards into 5 vowel boxes.
lp.prod: Make a class 'CVC book': each child creates a page with a picture, a CVC word and a sentence (The dog is big.). Read the pages aloud to a partner and compile as a book.
lp.rw: Read a short CVC reader (use 3 of the 6 sentence cards) and answer a yes/no question. Then write 5 dictated words and one sentence of your own. Fast finishers write 3 rhyming pairs (cat-hat).
lp.st: Phonics song 'Phonics Song 2' or 'The Letter A Song' from Music/Songs. Goodbye: exit ticket, each child says one new sentence at the door.
g: Run, read the CVC word and match it to a picture.
Spin, blend and check the word.
Sort pictures by their middle vowel sound.
Write the word the teacher says on a whiteboard.
Read a sentence card and do the action.
diff: Fast finishers: write 3 short CVC sentences and illustrate them.
Support: use letter cards with the vowel in a different colour; blend with finger tapping.
hw: Read 6 CVC sentences at home.
Write 3 CVC sentences of your own and draw them.
Find 5 CVC words on food or toy packages and bring them.
lp.tip: Short vowels are the hardest part for Arabic and French speakers (a/e, i/u). Say each sound with a mouth shape and let children feel it. Thanksgiving is an optional overlay.

Phonics CVC words, letter A (PPT game)
The Letter A Song - Learn the Alphabet

weeks.theme: Sounds and spelling 2: digraphs and blends
weeks.obj: read and spell words with sh, ch, th, ck, ng and common blends (st, sp, bl, cr); read and write 8 short sentences
weeks.lang: sh (ship, fish), ch (chair, chip), th (this, thin), ck (duck, sock), ng (ring, king); st, sp, bl, cr (stop, spin, black, crab); The fish is in the dish. / I can see a ship.
weeks.res: Phonics alphabet games (videos); Spelling games; What is a blend? (br, cr, dr, fr) video; Consonant blends posters
weeks.act: Digraph sort, blend and race, sentence reading and a 'sound story' with picture captions
weeks.hw: Find 6 words with sh, ch or th at home or in a book and write one sentence with 3 of them.

skills.L: Listen for sh, ch, th and sort words by sound
skills.S: Read digraph words and sentences aloud accurately
skills.R: Read short sentences and a 5-line text with digraphs
skills.W: Spell 8 dictated words and write 2 sentences

lp.wu: Sound snap: teacher holds up a word (ship, chair, thin); children snap if the word has sh, ch or th and say the sound. Warm up the mouth shapes with 'sh' (finger on lips) and 'th' (tongue out).
wuAlt: Whisper and shout: say the sound whisper (sh) or loud (ch) with the teacher's cards
Tongue twister: 'She sells shells' slowly, with a partner
lp.pres: Teach the digraphs with picture cards and mouth gestures: sh, ch, th, ck, ng. Show the 2 letters make 1 sound by drawing a loop. Then teach blends st, sp, bl, cr in words, slide the letters together.
presAlt: Sort the pictures: sh, ch or th boxes
Letter tiles: build 6 words with a digraph tile (sh+ip, ch+in)
lp.prac: Blend and race: pairs race to read a ladder of words (ship, shop, shell, chip, chop, chin, this, that, thin, duck, sock). Then read 8 sentence strips ('The sheep is in the shop.') and draw one.
pracAlt: Read and draw: read a sentence strip and draw it
Dictation pairs: one child reads a digraph word, the partner writes it
lp.ls: Teacher reads 8 words slowly (no recording needed): 'ship, chair, thick, duck, king, black, stop, spin.' Children write the digraph or blend they hear in a grid. Check with letter tiles.
lp.re: Digraph Bingo with pictures: the child covers a picture when the teacher says the word, and says the sound first (/sh/ - ship). First full line reads out the words.
lp.prod: Make a 'sound story': children draw 3 pictures (a ship, a fish, a chair) and write one sentence under each ('The ship is big.'). Share the story with a partner and ask 'What is it?'
lp.rw: Read a 5-line text 'The fish is in the dish. The duck is on the ship...' and answer 3 questions. Then dictation of 5 words and write 2 sentences. Fast finishers add a ch/sh/th tongue-twister.
lp.st: Phonics song 'Phonics Song 2 (new version)' from Music/Songs, then the blend chant. Goodbye: exit ticket, each child says one new sentence at the door.
g: Snap when the word has the target digraph.
Cover the pictures called and say the sound.
Read a word ladder as fast as you can without mistakes.
Read a word to a partner who writes it.
diff: Fast finishers: write 5 sentences with three digraph words each and underline the digraphs.
Support: give word cards with digraphs coloured; allow tapping out the sounds.
hw: Find 6 words with sh, ch or th and write 3 sentences.
Read the sound story to someone at home.
Practise the tongue twister and teach it to someone.
lp.tip: Reading and writing here is decoding accuracy, not speed: celebrate correct sounds. The th sound often becomes /s/ or /z/: model it with a visible tongue.

weeks.theme: Hobbies and sports: I like playing...
weeks.obj: name 12 hobbies and sports; say what I like, love and can do with -ing and can; ask and answer Do you like...? and Can you...?; use Do you play...? with short answers
weeks.lang: football, basketball, tennis, swimming, drawing, dancing, reading, cycling, chess, painting, computer games, karate; I like playing football. / I love swimming.; Can you swim? Yes, I can. / No, I can't.; Do you play tennis? Yes, I do. / No, I don't.; on Saturday
weeks.res: Sports lesson plan (actions and sports); Free time, hobbies and sports worksheets; Hobbies hidden picture game (PPT); Sports flashcards
weeks.act: Hobby survey and 'Find someone who' game, then a 'Hobby profile' poster
weeks.hw: Write 4 sentences about your hobbies: 'I like ___ing. I can ___. I don't like ___ing.'

skills.L: Listen to hobbies of 4 children and match them to names
skills.S: Ask and answer Do you like...? Can you...? Do you play...?
skills.R: Read a short hobby text and answer 4 questions
skills.W: Write 4 sentences about my hobbies

lp.wu: Hobby mime: children mime a hobby and the class guesses 'Do you like swimming?' 'Yes, I do!' Add the sentence 'I like swimming. I love dancing.'
wuAlt: Move to the corner: 4 corners for 'love, like, don't like, hate'; stand and say a sentence
Chain: 'I like football. She likes football and I like swimming.'
lp.pres: Present the hobbies and sports with the Sports flashcards or PPT. Model 'I like playing football. I love swimming.' (verb + -ing, with play for sports). Show can: 'Can you ride a bike? Yes, I can.' and 'Do you play chess? Yes, I do.' Chorus the three question forms.
presAlt: Hobby sort: cards into 'play' and 'go' and '-ing' lists (play football, go swimming)
Dialogue drill: A asks Do you like..., B answers
lp.prac: Hobby survey: each child asks 5 classmates 'Do you like swimming? Can you play chess?' and records answers on a grid. Report in groups 'Four children like swimming. Two children can't play chess.'
pracAlt: Find someone who: collect names that match hobby statements
Interview in pairs: ask 6 questions about weekend hobbies
lp.ls: Teacher reads aloud (no recording needed): 'My name is Ayoub. I like playing football and I love reading. I can't swim but I can ride a bike.' Children tick the right pictures on a hobby profile. Repeat with 3 more children.
lp.re: Hobby bingo with pictures and hobbies called in sentences; or 'Four corners' where children stand at the hobby corner they like and say a sentence.
lp.prod: Hobby profile poster: each child draws their hobbies and writes 4 sentences ('I like painting. I can ride a bike. I don't like chess.'). Present to a group and answer 'Do you play...?' questions.
lp.rw: Read a 5-line text about Lina's hobbies and answer 4 questions. Then write 4 sentences about your poster. Fast finishers write a dialogue (4 lines) asking about hobbies.
lp.st: Song 'Let's Go to the Beach' or an action song from Music/Songs. Goodbye: exit ticket, each child says one new sentence at the door.
g: Mime a hobby and the class guesses Do you like...?
Stand in the corner that matches your opinion and say why.
Collect names for hobbies and abilities.
Repeat what others like and add your own.
diff: Fast finishers: write a paragraph about a friend's hobbies in the third person (He likes... She can...).
Support: hobby word cards with pictures; sentence frames I like ___ing. I can ___.
hw: Write 4 sentences about your hobbies.
Interview a family member about their hobbies.
Draw a sports day poster with 4 sports and label them.
lp.tip: Present simple questions (Do you...) are a new step: use short answers only. Third-person -s is not required yet. Check that every child can find a hobby they like, including quiet ones (reading, drawing).

weeks.obj: name 6 habitats and 12 animals; say where an animal lives and what it eats (Camels live in the desert. They eat plants.); ask and answer Where does it live? What does it eat?; sort animals into herbivores and carnivores
weeks.lang: desert, jungle, forest, ocean, river, farm; camel, lion, monkey, whale, crocodile, bear, fish, frog, eagle, rabbit; Where does it live? It lives in the jungle.; What does it eat? It eats meat/plants/fish.; Lions live in Africa. They eat meat.; Do rabbits eat meat? No, they don't.
weeks.res: Animal flashcards; Animal games (printable); Animals hidden picture game (PPT); Sea animals vocabulary (video)
weeks.act: Habitat sort and animal fact cards: classify animals by home and food and present a 'Food chain' of 3 animals
weeks.hw: Write 4 sentences about an animal: where it lives and what it eats ('A frog lives near a river. It eats flies.').

skills.L: Listen to animal riddles and name the animal
skills.S: Ask and answer Where does it live? What does it eat?
skills.R: Read a 5-line animal fact card and answer 4 questions
skills.W: Write 4 sentences about an animal's home and food

lp.wu: Habitat corners: the teacher puts 4 corner signs (desert, jungle, ocean, forest); on a flashcard children run to the animal's home and say 'It lives in the ocean.'
wuAlt: Animal mime and guess: 'Is it a lion? Does it live in Africa?'
Habitat chant with 4 hand gestures
lp.pres: Present habitats and animals with the Animals flashcards and the 'What can it do, what does it have' PPT. Model 'Camels live in the desert. They eat plants.' using a table (animal, home, food). Teach carnivore/herbivore as picture words (meat, plants) only. Practise questions and short answers 'Does a rabbit eat meat? No, it doesn't.' (chunks).
presAlt: Habitat sort: put animal cards on 4 habitat posters and say the sentence
Diet match: match animals to their food cards
lp.prac: Habitat detectives in pairs: Child A has an animal card (home, food, 2 facts) and Child B asks 'Where does it live? What does it eat?' to guess. Then they fill a table for 4 animals and make a simple food chain: grass - rabbit - fox.
pracAlt: Information gap: partners have different halves of an animal table
Odd one out: 4 animals, 3 eat meat, say why with 'It eats plants.'
lp.ls: Teacher reads three riddles aloud (no recording needed): 'I live in the ocean. I'm very big. I eat small fish. What am I?' Children write or point to the animal and its home. Then the teacher says 4 facts and children tick true or false on a card.
lp.re: Habitat bingo and run: the teacher says 'It eats leaves and lives in a forest'; children run to the right corner and name the animal.
lp.prod: Animal fact poster: groups choose 3 animals from different habitats, draw them with their food and write 3 sentences each. Present as wildlife guides: 'This is a camel. It lives in the desert. It eats plants.'
lp.rw: Read a 5-line text about the desert and its animals ('Camels and snakes live in the desert...') and answer 4 questions. Then write 4 sentences about an animal. Fast finishers add 'It can...' and 'It has got...' (from Beginners).
lp.st: Song 'What Do You See?' (nature and animals) from Music/Songs, or the Biomes video from Videos/Videos for Children/Nature. Goodbye: exit ticket, each child says one new sentence at the door.
g: Run to the corner for the animal's home.
Guess the animal from home and food clues.
Match animals to the food they eat.
Find the animal that does not belong and say why.
Order cards to make a simple food chain.
diff: Fast finishers: write a longer fact file with home, food, size and one amazing fact.
Support: habitat and food picture cards with the sentence frame It lives in ___. It eats ___.
hw: Write 4 sentences about an animal.
Draw a food chain with 3 pictures and label it.
Ask someone at home: What does a cat eat? and write the answer.
lp.tip: This is a mini science lesson in English (CLIL): the language is where and what, not long scientific words. Third-person -s (lives, eats) is a chunk. Use only animals children know or can see in a picture.

weeks.theme: Healthy eating: healthy, unhealthy, How much and How many
weeks.obj: sort foods into healthy and unhealthy; say what I eat and drink in a day; ask and answer How much...? and How many...?; plan a healthy lunch with some and any
weeks.lang: healthy, unhealthy, fruit, vegetables, bread, rice, fish, eggs, milk, water, sweets, crisps, fizzy drinks; I eat/drink some... I don't eat any...; Is there any milk? Yes, there is. / Are there any eggs? No, there aren't.; How much water do you drink? How many apples do you eat?; a lot of, a little, a few; It's good for you.
weeks.res: Food flashcards; Food hidden picture game (PPT); Food bingo (printable)
weeks.act: Healthy plate challenge: design a healthy lunch and survey how many fruits and how much water classmates have
weeks.hw: Write what you ate yesterday (4 sentences) and say which food was healthy ('I ate/had some rice. It's healthy.').

skills.L: Listen to menus and tick healthy or unhealthy
skills.S: Ask and answer How much? How many? and Is there any?
skills.R: Read a short text about a healthy day and answer 4 questions
skills.W: Write 5 sentences about a healthy lunch with some / any

lp.wu: Food sort race: teams run to put food cards on a healthy or unhealthy poster and say 'Apples are healthy. Crisps are unhealthy.'
wuAlt: Memory chain: 'I eat some rice and some fish...'
Mime: mime eating or drinking a food and guess
lp.pres: Present healthy and unhealthy foods with the Food flashcards and the Healthy Eating video. Teach countable/uncountable with sorting (an apple, some milk). Model 'How many apples? How much water?' and 'Is there any milk? There isn't any bread.' Teach quantity phrases a lot of, a little, a few with small objects.
presAlt: Sort the cards into countable and uncountable
Plate game: put foods on a paper plate and describe it
lp.prac: Healthy plate challenge in groups: design a healthy lunch (6 items) and describe it ('There is some rice. There are two apples. There isn't any fizzy drink.'). Then each group surveys classmates: 'How many apples do you eat in a week?' 'How much water do you drink?' and charts the results.
pracAlt: Fridge detective: look at a fridge picture for 20 seconds and answer Is there any...? Are there any...?
Menu interview: ask 3 friends what they eat for breakfast
lp.ls: Teacher reads aloud (no recording needed) three daily menus: 'For breakfast I have some bread and milk. For lunch I eat rice and fish...' Children tick H (healthy) or U (unhealthy) next to each menu. Then 4 quantity questions: 'How many eggs are there?' (picture check).
lp.re: Fridge detective: show a fridge picture for 20 seconds, hide it, and ask 'Is there any cheese? Are there any apples?' Children answer in short answers, then redraw the fridge.
lp.prod: Healthy lunch poster: each group draws a plate of 6 foods and writes 5 sentences ('There is some fish. There aren't any sweets. It's healthy.'). Present to another group, who ask How much/How many.
lp.rw: Read a 6-line text 'A healthy day' (Hamza has some bread and milk for breakfast...) and answer 4 questions. Then write 5 sentences about your lunch. Fast finishers add 'I don't eat much sugar.' (optional).
lp.st: Song 'Food Song' or 'Yummy Food Song' from Music/Songs, or the 'Healthy Eating in English' video from Videos/Videos for Children/Food. Goodbye: exit ticket, each child says one new sentence at the door.
g: Sort food cards into healthy and unhealthy.
Memorise a fridge picture and answer Is there any...?
Put foods on a paper plate and describe it.
I eat some rice and some fish and...
Ask How much? How many? and make a chart.
diff: Fast finishers: write a weekly healthy menu with 7 days and 2 meals.
Support: food picture cards with sentence frames There is some ___. There aren't any ___.
hw: Write what you ate yesterday and say which was healthy.
Make a healthy shopping list with 6 items.
Count the fruits and vegetables you eat in a day and tell someone.
lp.tip: Some/any, How much and How many are the grammar step; make them physical with real or paper food. Keep health talk positive: no one is 'bad' for eating sweets. Check cultural food customs and allergies. Christmas is an optional overlay; the lesson stays on healthy eating.

weeks.theme: Money and the market: How much is it?
weeks.obj: count in tens to 100 and say 21-99; ask and answer How much is it? and How much are they? in dirhams; buy and sell at a class market with Can I have..., please?; write a price list
weeks.lang: ten, twenty... one hundred; 25, 36, 47, 58; How much is it? It's twenty dirhams. / How much are the apples? They're ten dirhams a kilo.; Can I have two kilos of tomatoes, please? Here you are. Thank you.; cheap, expensive; kilo, bottle, box
weeks.res: Counting games (7 up, fizz buzz); Mixed vocabulary games (Jeopardy, Sleeping Pandas); Role-playing games; Shopping vocabulary (poster); Shopping dialogue (poster)
weeks.act: Class market role play: sellers with price lists and buyers with 50 dirhams, then a price list poster
weeks.hw: Write the price of 5 things you know in dirhams ('The bread is two dirhams.') and ask someone at home about one price.

skills.L: Listen to prices and write them down
skills.S: Role play at the market with How much is it? Can I have...?
skills.R: Read price tags and a short market dialogue
skills.W: Write a price list with 5 items and 3 sentences

lp.wu: Count by tens in a circle (10, 20, 30...), then by tens with a clap. Teacher calls 'Twenty-three!' and children show the number with fingers on two hands (20 + 3).
wuAlt: Number race: two teams, teacher says 'Forty-five', first runner touches the numeral
Whisper numbers around the circle and check the last one
lp.pres: Present tens and 21-99 with a hundred square and place-value cards (twenty + five = twenty-five). Introduce prices with realia and dirham price tags: 'How much is it? It's twenty dirhams.' Drill with 4 items.
presAlt: Price tag matching: pairs match items to price tags and ask 'How much is the ball?'
Number puzzle: put tens and units cards together (30 + 6 = 36) and read them
lp.prac: Class market: half the children are sellers with 4 priced items (real or pictures), half are buyers with 50 play dirhams; buyers ask 'How much is it?' and 'Can I have two kilos, please?', then say 'Thank you' and swap. Add 'I'd like...' as an optional stretch.
pracAlt: Market dialogue pairs: read and complete a 5-line dialogue with prices
Price hunt: the teacher gives prices, children find the item on a price list
lp.ls: Teacher reads six prices in dirhams (no recording needed): 'The ball is fifteen dirhams.' Children write 15. Add a trap: 'fifty' and 'fifteen'. Check in pairs.
lp.re: Market bingo: each child has a 3x3 card of prices; the teacher says a price in words ('forty-five') and children cover it; winners read their line aloud. Then 'cheap or expensive?' cards.
lp.prod: Price list poster: groups make a market stall with 6 items and prices and write 4 sentences ('The tomatoes are ten dirhams a kilo. The bread is two dirhams.'). Present as sellers and answer 'How much is it?'
lp.rw: Read 4 price tags and a short market dialogue (How much are the oranges? They're eight dirhams a kilo.) and match them. Then write the price list and 3 sentences. Fast finishers add a total for a shopping list.
lp.st: Counting song of choice from Music/Songs (Let's Count to 20). Goodbye: exit ticket, each child says one new sentence at the door.
g: Sellers and buyers practise How much is it?
Teams run to touch the numeral called in words.
Find an item on a price list from the teacher's clue.
Cover the prices called in words.
Cover tens and numbers called from 10 to 100.
diff: Fast finishers: write a shopping list with 4 prices and a total.
Support: use number cards with words, and play money with printed numerals.
hw: Write the price of 5 things you know in dirhams.
Ask someone at home how much one thing costs and report in English.
Draw a price tag poster for 3 items.
lp.tip: Use Moroccan market items and real coins or notes if you can. Prices in tens and teens are the main pitfall: practise fifteen vs fifty. New Year is an optional overlay this week.

skills.S: Retell the story with 4 sentences
skills.R: Read the story's 6 sentences and answer true/false
skills.W: Write one sentence for each picture (4 sentences)

wuAlt: Rapid fire: teacher shows a flashcard from weeks 2-13 and children say the word plus a sentence

Question round: who is big? who is small? who helps?

g: Say the word and a sentence for the flashcard shown.
Put story pictures in order and tell it.
Answer questions as the lion or the mouse.
Mime animals, toys or objects for the team.
diff: Fast finishers: write a mini play with 3 characters and 6 lines.
Support: use story pictures with the sentence strips to put in order.
hw: Draw 4 pictures of the story and write one sentence under each.
Tell the story to someone at home.
Write 3 true and 3 false sentences about you (country, birthday, hobbies).
lp.tip: Use Review weeks to spot who needs support before assessment. The story is a vehicle for reading: finish with a sentence strip order task. Week 15 is the Semester 1 assessment: prepare the observation checklist.

lp.st: Closing ceremony: each child collects the passport and says one thing they are proud of. Preview Semester 2 (town, transport, weather, health, plans, comparing). Goodbye: exit ticket, each child says one new sentence at the door.
g: Six known games with the teacher's checklist.
A stamp per station on a personal passport.
The spinner chooses the next review game.
Name 5 items on the wall poster gallery.
diff: All: this week is the differentiation; the checklist records each child at their own level.
Second adult if available: one runs stations while you observe and tick.
hw: Show your sticker passport to someone at home.
Teach someone at home one S1 game.
Find 5 English words in your home and bring a list next week.
lp.tip: Tick the checklist during play, never as a table test. If a child freezes, come back later. Keep the tone festive. Send the Semester 1 reports home this week.

weeks.obj: name 10 places in a town; say where places are with next to/between/opposite; ask and answer Where's the...? and give 3 simple directions (go straight on, turn left/right)

weeks.res: Directions flashcards (map); Directions lesson plan; Giving directions worksheets; Giving directions (PPT game); Buildings hidden picture game (PPT)
weeks.act: Town map game: give and follow directions from the school to a place, then draw and describe my town
weeks.hw: Draw a map of your street with 4 places and write 4 sentences with next to and opposite.

skills.L: Listen to directions and follow a route on a map
skills.S: Ask Where's the...? and give directions with go straight on and turn left/right
skills.R: Read a short text about a town and answer 4 questions
skills.W: Write 4 sentences about places on a map and 2 directions

lp.wu: Direction game in the room: the teacher says 'Go straight on... Turn left... Stop!' and children walk as instructed; later a child becomes the caller with a classroom map.
wuAlt: Mr Wolf: 'What's the time?' game adapted to places: 'It's the bank!'
Map memory: look at a town map for 30 seconds and write the places you remember
lp.pres: Present places with the Directions Map and town flashcards. Model 'Where's the park? It's next to the school. It's opposite the library. It's between the bank and the shop.' Then directions: 'Go straight on. Turn left. Turn right. It's on the right.' with a floor map and gestures.
presAlt: Floor town: children walk on a floor map and follow directions
Map gap: partners have maps with different places and ask Where's the...?
lp.prac: Map pair task: Child A reads directions from the school to a secret place on the map ('Go straight on. Turn left. Where are you?'), Child B follows with a finger and names the place. Swap with new routes. Draw their own route and give directions.
pracAlt: Treasure map: follow directions to find the treasure on the map
Draw my street: partners describe their street and the other draws
lp.ls: Teacher reads aloud (no recording needed): 'You are at the school. Go straight on. Turn left at the bank. It is next to the post office. Where are you?' Children trace the route on a map and name the place. Repeat with 3 routes.
lp.re: Robot directions: a child is a robot and a partner gives directions to a place in the room ('Go straight on. Turn right. Stop!'). Check the target.
lp.prod: Make a map of an imaginary town in groups with 8 places, then give each other 3 directions to follow and describe where 3 places are. Present to another group.
lp.rw: Read a 5-line text 'My town' (There is a park next to my school...) and answer 4 questions. Then write 4 sentences about the map and 2 directions. Fast finishers add a short dialogue (Excuse me, where's the ...?).
lp.st: Song 'Where Are You Going? Places Song' from Music/Songs or the video 'Prepositions of movement' from Videos. Goodbye: exit ticket, each child says one new sentence at the door.
g: Give directions to move a robot child to a target.
Follow directions on a map to find the treasure.
Ask Where's the...? to complete a map.
Walk a floor map by following directions.
Remember the places on a map and write them.
diff: Fast finishers: write directions from home to school in 5 steps.
Support: use arrows with direction words, a map with pictures.
hw: Draw a map of your street with 4 places and write 4 sentences.
Give directions from your door to the kitchen in English to someone at home.
Teach someone left and right with a game.
lp.tip: Left and right need physical practice: use arrow cards and a floor map. Keep the directions short (3 steps). Next to and between come back in the bedroom week.
